text:
Predicates:
City(x) ::: x is a city.
State(x) ::: x is a state.
In(x, y) ::: x is in y.
Country(x) ::: x is a country.
US(x) ::: x is in U.S.
Premises:
City(billings) ∧ In(billings, montana) ∧ In(montana, us) ::: Billings is a city in the state of Montana in U.S.
In(montana, us) ∧ (City(butte) ∨ City(helena) ∨ City(missoula)) ∧ In(butte, montana) ∧ In(helena, montana) ∧ In(missoula, montana) ::: The state of Montana includes the cities of Butte, Helena, and Missoula.
City(whiteSulphurSprings) ∧ City(butte) ∧ In(whiteSulphurSprings, montana) ∧ In(butte, montana) ∧ In(montana, us) ::: White Sulphur Springs and Butte are cities in the same state in U.S.
City(stPierre) ∧ ¬In(stPierre, montana) ::: The city of St Pierre is not in the state of Montana.
∀x (City(x) ∧ In(x, butte) → ¬In(x, stPierre)) ::: Any city in Butte is not in St Pierre.
∀x (City(x) ∧ In(x, us) → (∃y (State(y) ∧ In(x, y)) ↔ ¬(x = bristol ∨ x = texarkana ∨ x = texhoma ∨ x = unionCity))) ::: A city can only be in one state in U.S. except for Bristol, Texarkana, Texhoma and Union City.
Conclusion:
In(butte, stPierre) ⊕ In(butte, montana) ::: Butte and St Pierre are in the same state.
